title: add dynamic-profile-sampling and onboarding checklist generator
author: Maya Singh
release_notes: Adds dynamic sampling engine for long-tail model profiling, a machine-readable onboarding checklist generator, and a changelog composer hook. Backwards-compatible metadata keys added. No runtime behavior changes for existing registry consumers.
description: Motivation: onboarding long-tail variants (small, quantized, distillations) has been brittle because our profiling pipeline assumed uniform sampling. This PR introduces a dynamic-profile-sampling engine that picks example slices by usage heat, token-length distribution, and a rare-case weight to produce representative performance profiles with fewer runs. It also supplies a machine-readable onboarding checklist generator that emits actionable items for reviewers (missing metadata, required evals, compatibility flags) and an optional changelog composer hook that synthesizes concise release notes from profile deltas. Implementation summary: 1) profile_sampler.py implements a multi-criteria sampler with pluggable heuristic weights and deterministic seeding for repeatability; 2) onboard_checklist.go adds a generator that consumes metadata and evaluation results and outputs a checklist JSON that the UI and CLI surface; 3) changelog_composer.go provides a configurable template engine that turns delta summaries and perf-regressions into draft release notes; 4) added lightweight telemetry events and unit tests for sampler edge cases; 5) updated docs/onboarding.md and examples with recommended sampling presets and rollout guidance. Backwards compatibility: sampler defaults to the legacy uniform mode unless the model manifest sets "sampling.strategy": "dynamic". Checklist output only augments existing review flows and is gated behind a feature flag. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to canary workspace, followed by a 2-week telemetry bake to validate representativeness and cost impact. Related work: complements ENG-5128 (profiling pipeline refactor) and should reduce average profiling runs by ~40% on preliminary experiments. Notes: I intentionally kept the default weights conservative to avoid biasing short-tail production models. Open questions: should we add an automated calibration step that tunes weights based on historical evaluation results?
